question: Crossing the midline on imaging is a characteristic feature of neuroblastoma rather than Wilms tumor, because neuroblastoma arises from the adrenal medulla or sympathetic chain and encases retroperitoneal vessels as it grows.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The single most useful differentiating imaging feature at presentation is midline crossing: neuroblastoma crosses (and encases great vessels); Wilms tumor stays within the kidney and does not cross. A suprarenal location and calcification on KUB also favour neuroblastoma.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Neuroblastoma classically crosses the midline as it arises from midline sympathetic structures and encases the aorta and its branches. Wilms tumor arises intrinsically within the renal parenchyma and displaces rather than encases vessels, and rarely crosses the midline.
